proposal.title: 2. SSG General Ledger — Define the native C/TUI General Ledger port and its acceptance contract
proposal.reason: Replace the former BPI scenario with the author-requested independent SSG General Ledger partnership. Use the confirmed story dates: agreement 1977-07-28, team/development 1977-08-12, vanilla CP/M/CBASIC release 1978-01-15 and joint AION C/General Ledger Aurelia launch on the morning of 1978-06-06. SSG retains application ownership and sales; AION funds bounded porting and later networking work, not an equity investment. Preserve stable legacy record IDs for reference and review continuity; displayed identities and product scope are SSG General Ledger. Exact original GL/runtime revisions and speed ratios remain unverified. See review_evidence/ssg-general-ledger for source distinctions, scope and validation.

chapters.description: The suite is implemented in AION C around a relational base engine, the Logix TUI and native FlexiBUS printing. General Accounting covers ledger, simplified receivables/payables, payroll integration and balance sheets. Accounts Receivable tracks customers, open invoices, payments and statements; Accounts Payable tracks vendors, liabilities, cash-flow obligations and cheque printing. Inventory Control handles stock, purchase orders, movement journals and profitability. Payroll handles employee hours, local/federal withholding, benefits and payroll cheques.

Selected balances or monthly totals are exported as versioned delimited text with named columns, period, currency, account identifiers, decimal amounts and control totals. Close BPI before loading Abacus to use these as independent planning inputs; there is no automatic write-back, simultaneous execution or live database link. Reconcile counts/totals and test rounding, quoting, disk-full handling, memory and save/reopen; label prepared demonstration data.

The implementation uses {portable_api_id}. Keep application/document algorithms separate from platform adapters; query display dimensions and attributes, use semantic colours and clipping, and handle allocation failures with bounded buffers and banked-object handles. Persistent records are explicitly encoded and versioned rather than raw structures or pointers. Recompile and adapt OS-specific modules for another target, then test its resource limits; source portability does not extend the list of qualified hosts.

This application suite targets Z80/CP/M on {host_base_computer_aurelia} and {host_base_computer_aurelia_plus}. The recorded installed-RAM requirement is {minimum_ram_kib} KiB. It requires {runtime_cpm_aurelia}. The edition is delivered on diskette. Application workspace and ROM footprint remain unspecified.

chapters.description: General Ledger maintains custom charts of accounts, departments, journal entries, corrections, period balances and financial reports. The AION C implementation uses versioned record files and bounded buffers; the standalone release does not depend on a general relational database or include receivables, payables, inventory or payroll modules. Performance-critical string, record and decimal routines may be written in assembly and linked through the published ABI. Application code and state run in RAM; shared assembler-written TUI code executes from the system ROM through bank-safe calls.

Selected account balances and monthly totals become independent Abacus planning inputs through a versioned disk file. Close General Ledger before loading Abacus; there is no automatic ledger write-back or live database link. Reconcile counts and control totals, validate decimals and quoting, and test disk-full, memory exhaustion and save/reopen. Label prepared demonstration data.

The implementation uses {portable_api_id}. Keep application/document algorithms separate from platform adapters; query display dimensions and attributes, use semantic colours and clipping, and handle allocation failures with bounded buffers and banked-object handles. Persistent records are explicitly encoded and versioned rather than raw structures or pointers. Recompile and adapt OS-specific modules for another target, then test its resource limits; source portability does not extend the list of qualified hosts.

This General Ledger application targets Z80/CP/M on {host_base_computer_aurelia} and {host_base_computer_aurelia_plus}. The recorded installed-RAM requirement is {minimum_ram_kib} KiB. It requires {runtime_cpm_aurelia}. The edition is delivered on diskette. Application workspace and ROM footprint remain unspecified. One distribution diskette is the package assumption; installation, working-data space and any media exchanges require qualification.

Use explicit decimal or sufficiently wide scaled-integer routines with documented range, rounding and overflow handling. Reconcile CBASIC reference reports and cases exercising 14-digit precision before timing the port. Preserve posting and recovery semantics. Test maximum balances, reversals, period closing, interrupted updates, disk-full handling and backup restoration. On-disk values use explicit encodings, not raw C structures.

Bounded text fields, lists, account tables, selection dropdowns and buttons use Tab/Shift-Tab, shortcuts, shared selection/editing and copy/paste. Composite controls may be SDK helpers over ROM primitives. Text mode is the baseline; bitmap rendering is optional only on qualified configurations. Measure native code, selected C/assembly libraries and ROM TUI call/bank-switch costs. Compare identical datasets and financial outputs on the same hardware; report CPU work separately from disk and printer waits without a promised speed ratio.

after.name: SSG General Ledger — CP/M edition
after.description: SSG General Ledger for Aurelia and Aurelia+ uses a native Z80 AION C implementation and the shared ROM TUI; its Aurelia release is on 6 June 1978. SSG owns and licenses the application and maintains specialist support. The package covers General Ledger, not a five-module accounting suite. Selected ledger balances and period totals can be exported to Abacus through a reconciled, versioned disk file. AION engineering sponsorship and Logix distribution confer no application ownership.

specification.description: SSG owns and licenses General Ledger.
Defines the CP/M implementation, ledger functions, platform support and delivery contents.
Defines independent SSG ownership and the development, distribution and training relationship.

BPI applications share a relational database so accounting, receivables, payables, inventory and payroll can use a consistent data foundation. The specification defines that architecture without asserting unrecorded capacity or throughput.

A relational database engine provides the common data foundation for BPI business applications.

Accounting, receivables, payables, inventory and payroll share structured business data.

after.name: SSG General Ledger data and transaction architecture
after.description: Ledger file and numeric contracts, with a separately qualified client/server transaction service for the later network edition.

specification.description: Standalone SSG General Ledger uses explicitly encoded chart, journal and balance records, bounded access buffers, consistent decimal rules and auditable corrections. Its 1978 C/TUI port preserves the original application semantics without requiring a relational database engine or additional accounting modules.

The later client/server edition moves ledger validation, posting, queries and durable transactions to the server. Its defined relational service, logging, checkpoint, duplicate-request handling and restoration design require independent qualification; these capabilities are not attributed to the January or June 1978 standalone releases.
